title: Diff Viewer — Line-by-Line Text Diff with Line Numbers
desc: Compare an original and a modified text in one column: removed lines in red, added lines in green, changed words highlighted, both line numbers.
ui: Diff Viewer Compare two texts and highlight differences Original Modified Ignore whitespace Ignore case Compare

about.heading: About Diff Viewer
about.text: Diff Viewer lists the differences between two texts in a single column, like a patch: each line is marked unchanged, removed (-) or added (+), with its number in the original and in the modified text. It uses the Myers algorithm (jsdiff library), so one inserted line is shown as one addition instead of shifting everything below it. When a line is replaced, the words that changed are highlighted inside both versions. Options ignore letter case, or spaces at line ends and the amount of space between words. Windows and Unix line endings compare as equal. Text Comparator shows the same comparison in two columns.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Output of the page’s own comparison code; [-…-] and {+…+} stand for the words highlighted in red and green. Original, then Modified Original: red The cat sat on the mat blue Modified: red The dog sat on the mat blue green Result (original line no., modified line no., line) 1 1 red 2 - The [-cat-] sat on the mat 2 + The {+dog+} sat on the mat 3 3 blue 4 + green

howto: Paste the first version in "Original" and the new version in "Modified".
Tick "Ignore whitespace" so that re-indented lines are not listed as removed and added, and "Ignore case" for changes of capitals only.
Click "Compare"; the button stays grey until both boxes contain text.
Read the list: a red line was removed, a green line was added, and the two numbers on the left give its line in each text.
howtoHeading: How to compare two texts line by line

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input Two pasted texts; there is no file upload Options Ignore case; Ignore whitespace (trims line ends and treats a run of spaces as one space) Line endings Windows, Unix and old Mac line breaks are treated as the same Result One column with original and modified line numbers and word highlights; no download Text size The tool sets no size cap; above 1,000,000 characters a box shows only its first 20,000 characters, and the comparison still uses all of it

Where your texts are compared.heading: Where your texts are compared
Where your texts are compared.text: Both texts are compared by code running in this page and are never sent to our servers or stored. The comparison library is downloaded with the page code the first time you click Compare. The result disappears when you reload, so copy what you need from it first.

faq.q: Can it ignore indentation changes?
faq.a: Yes. With "Ignore whitespace" ticked, a line whose indentation went from 2 to 4 spaces is listed once as unchanged, with its old and new line numbers, and a tab compares equal to a space. A space inserted inside a word still counts as a change.

faq.q: Does it show which words changed inside a line?
faq.a: Yes. When removed lines are followed by added ones, they are paired in order and the words that differ are highlighted inside each pair: red in the old line, green in the new one. Lines added or removed without a partner are shown whole.

faq.q: Can I see the two texts side by side?
faq.a: No. Diff Viewer shows one list with both line numbers, the way a patch reads. Text Comparator, in the text tools, uses the same comparison engine and options and shows the two texts in two columns.

faq.q: Do Windows line endings show up as differences?
faq.a: No. CRLF, CR and LF line breaks are all turned into the same break before comparing, so a file saved on Windows and the same file saved on Linux compare as identical.

tips: Comparing two versions of a JSON file? Format both with JSON Formatter first so that each value sits on its own line.

title: .env to JSON Converter — dotenv Rules, Both Directions
desc: Paste a .env file to get a JSON object, or a JSON object to get .env lines. Parsed like dotenv, with optional types and variable expansion.
ui: .env to JSON Convert .env files to JSON and back Input Output Convert numbers, true/false and null to JSON types Expand ${VAR} references .env to JSON JSON to .env Copy

about.heading: About .env to JSON
about.text: .env to JSON converts a .env file into a JSON object, and a JSON object back into .env lines. It follows the rules of the dotenv library: an optional export, KEY=value or KEY: value, single quotes kept literally, double quotes turning \n into a line break, backticks, quoted values over several lines and # comments outside quotes. By default every value stays a string; options give typed numbers, true, false and null, and expand ${VAR} references. Lines that are not variables are listed by number. Both directions run in your browser.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A .env file with export, a comment, an inline comment and a line that is not a variable, converted with both options unticked; the line under the JSON is the note the page shows: .env export APP_NAME="My App" PORT=3000 # database DB_URL=postgres://localhost/app # local only GREETING="Hello\nWorld" RAW='$HOME stays' not a variable JSON { "APP_NAME": "My App", "PORT": "3000", "DB_URL": "postgres://localhost/app", "GREETING": "Hello\nWorld", "RAW": "$HOME stays" } 5 variables — line 7 is not KEY=value and was skipped

howto: Paste your .env content, or a JSON object, into "Input".
Tick "Convert numbers, true/false and null to JSON types" or "Expand ${VAR} references" if you need them.
Click ".env to JSON", or "JSON to .env" for the other direction.
Click "Copy", or "Download": the file is named env.json in both directions.
howtoHeading: How to convert a .env file to JSON

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input .env text, or a JSON object Output JSON object with two-space indentation, or .env lines Repeated keys the last definition wins

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: Both directions run in your browser; the variables you paste, secrets included, are not uploaded, and the result is only shown on this page. If an error occurs, for example invalid JSON, its wording is reported to us with quoted text masked, with the tool name and browser version, so keep secrets out of key names.

faq.q: Does it expand ${OTHER_VAR} references?
faq.a: Yes, when "Expand ${VAR} references" is ticked: ${VAR}, ${VAR:-default} and $VAR take the value of a variable defined earlier in the file, as dotenv-expand does, and \$ keeps a literal dollar sign. With the option ticked, single-quoted values are expanded too.

faq.q: Are numbers and booleans typed?
faq.a: No, not by default, since .env values are text. Tick "Convert numbers, true/false and null to JSON types" and 3000 becomes a number and true, false and null become JSON values, while 007 and 1.10 stay strings because a number would change them.

faq.q: Are comments kept?
faq.a: No. A line starting with #, or # after an unquoted value, is a comment and is dropped, so JSON to .env cannot restore it; a # inside quotes stays part of the value. A line that is neither a comment nor a variable is reported by its number.

faq.q: Can JSON to .env handle nested objects?
faq.a: Yes. A nested object or array is written as JSON text inside quotes, and each value gets the quoting that makes dotenv read it back unchanged; a value mixing ', ", \ and ` together is refused, since no .env quoting can hold it, and null gives an empty value. Keys may use only letters, digits, _, . and -.

title: Excel to CSV — Every Sheet, Comma or Semicolon, XLSX/XLS/ODS
desc: Convert an .xlsx, .xls or .ods workbook to CSV, one file per sheet and zipped if there are several. Choose comma, semicolon, tab or pipe. In your browser.
ui: Excel to CSV Convert Excel files to CSV Supports workbooks up to 150,000 rows (including the header row, files up to 90 MB). The conversion runs in a background worker; the Cancel button stops it. Separator Comma , Semicolon ; (Excel in most of Europe) Tab Pipe | Decimal comma (3,14 — with the semicolon, for Excel in Europe) Add a UTF-8 BOM (Excel then reads accents correctly) Click or drop an Excel or ODS file here Choose an Excel or ODS file

about.heading: About Excel to CSV
about.text: Excel to CSV turns each sheet of an .xlsx, .xls or .ods workbook into CSV. A workbook with one sheet gives one .csv file; with several sheets you get a .zip holding one .csv per sheet, named after the sheet, hidden sheets included. Cells are written as values: formulas give the result saved in the file, dates become ISO text such as 2024-01-15, and numbers with a format of their own, such as a percentage or a dollar amount, are written as Excel shows them; colors and fonts are dropped. Options set the separator, a decimal comma for European Excel and a byte order mark (UTF-8 BOM). Conversion starts as soon as you choose the file, in your browser.

example.heading: Example

howto: Set "Separator" first, and tick "Decimal comma" or "Add a UTF-8 BOM" if you need them: they apply to the next file you choose.
Choose an .xlsx, .xls or .ods file in the upload area; the conversion starts at once and "Cancel" stops it.
If the workbook has several sheets, their names are listed while it is read.
Click "Download" to save converted.csv, or converted.zip with one .csv per sheet.

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input XLSX, XLS or ODS workbook Output CSV for one sheet, ZIP of CSV files for several On a computer up to 90 MB and 150,000 rows, all sheets together On phones, iPhone and iPad up to 30 MB and 50,000 rows, all sheets together Separators comma, semicolon, tab or pipe

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: The workbook is opened and converted by a background worker in your browser, with the SheetJS library; it is not uploaded, and the CSV or ZIP is created in the page. Should an error happen, we get its text without the file name or quoted content, along with the tool name and the browser name and version.

faq.q: Do formulas come out as their results?
faq.a: Yes. Each formula cell is written with the result saved in the workbook, so =B2*2 gives 25 in the CSV, not the formula text. Colors, fonts and comments are dropped, but a number format such as a percentage or a currency is kept in the text.

faq.q: Can I make a CSV for Excel in France or Germany?
faq.a: Yes. Choose "Semicolon" in "Separator", tick "Decimal comma" so numbers read 12,5, and tick "Add a UTF-8 BOM" so Excel opens accents correctly. Set these before choosing the file, because the conversion starts as soon as the file is picked.

faq.q: Are all sheets converted?
faq.a: Yes, hidden sheets included. With more than one sheet you download converted.zip, holding one .csv per sheet named after it; characters a file name cannot hold, such as < > | or a double quote, become underscores, and a repeated name gets (2).

faq.q: Are dates written as numbers?
faq.a: No. A cell formatted as a date is written as ISO 8601 text, 2024-01-15, or 2024-02-29T13:45:00 when it has a time, also for workbooks on the 1904 date system of old Mac Excel.

faq.q: How large can the workbook be?
faq.a: 90 MB and 150,000 rows across all sheets on a computer, 30 MB and 50,000 rows on phones, iPhone and iPad. A workbook has to be read whole before any row exists, so split a bigger one into several files first.

tips: To get JSON instead, with one array of rows per sheet, use Excel to JSON.

title: Excel to JSON — Each Sheet as an Array of Row Objects
desc: Convert an .xlsx, .xls, .ods or .csv file to JSON: one array per sheet, first row as keys, dates as ISO text and empty cells as null. In your browser.
ui: Excel to JSON Convert Excel files to JSON Supports workbooks up to 150,000 rows across all sheets (files up to 90 MB). The conversion runs in a background worker; the Cancel button stops it. Click or drop an Excel, ODS, or CSV file here Choose an Excel, ODS, or CSV file

about.heading: About Excel to JSON
about.text: Excel to JSON reads an .xlsx, .xls or .ods workbook, or a .csv file, and writes one JSON object whose keys are the sheet names. Each sheet becomes an array of row objects whose keys come from the sheet's first row, and every row has the same keys: an empty cell gives null. Date cells become ISO 8601 text, formulas give their saved result, and emoji saved by pandas or openpyxl are kept. A .csv file is read as plain text, so every value stays a string and its sheet is called Sheet1. Conversion starts when you choose the file, in your browser.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A workbook with two sheets, Prices (date cells and formulas) and Notes (one empty cell), and the JSON the tool returns: Workbook Sheet Prices: Item | Price | Sold on | Total Tea | 12.5 | 2024-01-15 (date cell) | =B2*2 → 25 Coffee, ground | 1234.5 | 2024-02-15 (date cell) | =B3*2 → 2469 Sheet Notes: Name | Note Ann | (empty) Bob | call back JSON { "Prices": [ { "Item": "Tea", "Price": 12.5, "Sold on": "2024-01-15", "Total": 25 }, { "Item": "Coffee, ground", "Price": 1234.5, "Sold on": "2024-02-15", "Total": 2469 } ], "Notes": [ { "Name": "Ann", "Note": null }, { "Name": "Bob", "Note": "call back" } ] }

howto: Choose an .xlsx, .xls, .ods or .csv file in the upload area; the conversion starts on its own.
If the workbook has several sheets, their names appear while it is read, and "Cancel" stops the work.
Click "Download" to save converted.json, indented with two spaces.

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input XLSX, XLS, ODS or CSV file Output JSON object with one array of row objects per sheet On a computer up to 90 MB and 150,000 rows across all sheets On phones, iPhone and iPad up to 30 MB and 50,000 rows across all sheets

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: Your spreadsheet is read by a background worker in your browser with the SheetJS library and is not uploaded. What can reach us is an error report: the error text after file names and quoted text are removed, the tool name, and the name and version of your browser.

faq.q: Are empty cells included?
faq.a: Yes, as null. Every row of a sheet has the same keys, so code that reads a Note property finds null instead of a missing key. Rows that are completely empty are skipped.

faq.q: Are dates converted to text?
faq.a: Yes, to ISO 8601: 2024-01-15, or 2024-02-29T13:45:00 when the cell has a time, with no time zone added. Without this step an Excel date would come out as a serial number such as 45306.

faq.q: Can I choose which sheets to convert?
faq.a: No. Every sheet is converted, hidden ones included, each under its own name in the JSON. Delete the arrays you do not need afterwards, or save the sheets you want as a separate workbook first.

faq.q: Are duplicate column headers kept?
faq.a: Yes. When two columns share a header such as name, the second one becomes name_1 in each row object, so no value is overwritten.

faq.q: How big can the file be?
faq.a: 90 MB and 150,000 rows, counting all sheets, on a computer; 30 MB and 50,000 rows on phones, iPhone and iPad. Split a larger workbook into several files and convert them one by one.

tips: For CSV files instead of JSON, one per sheet, use Excel to CSV.

The tool sets no file size cap: large files are read in pieces. Text Files Algorithms Common MD5 SHA-1 SHA-256 SHA-512 SHA-2 and SHA-3 SHA-224 SHA-384 SHA3-256 SHA3-512 Keccak-256 (Ethereum) Other BLAKE2b-512 BLAKE3 RIPEMD-160 Checksums CRC32 CRC32C xxHash64 XXH3-64 XXH128 Select all Defaults None Output Hex, lowercase Hex, UPPERCASE Base64 HMAC secret key (optional) Expected hash, to verify (optional)

about.heading: About Hash Generator
about.text: Hash Generator computes 17 hashes and checksums (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-512, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, RIPEMD-160, CRC32, CRC32C, xxHash64, XXH3-64 and XXH128) for typed text or for files. Text is hashed as UTF-8 while you type. Files are read in 8 MiB pieces by background workers, several files in one run, and the tool sets no size cap. Paste a published checksum to see which ticked algorithm matches, add an HMAC key to sign data, and save file results as checksums.txt. Web Workers in your own tab compute every hash.

howto: Choose "Text" or "Files", then tick the algorithms you need: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 and CRC32 are ticked at first, and "Select all" ticks every one.
Type or paste text and the results appear as you type; for files, drop or choose them, then click the button that starts with Hash and counts the files you added.
To verify a download, paste its published checksum into "Expected hash, to verify (optional)": the matching value turns green.
"Copy" copies one value; in Files mode, "Copy all" copies every checksum line and "Download" saves them as checksums.txt.

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Algorithms 17: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-512, Keccak-256, BLAKE2b-512, BLAKE3, RIPEMD-160, CRC32, CRC32C, xxHash64, XXH3-64, XXH128 Output format Hex lowercase, hex uppercase or Base64 on screen; checksums.txt always uses lowercase hex File size The tool sets no cap: files are streamed in 8 MiB pieces Web Crypto path SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 use your browser's native code for files up to 700 MiB on a computer and 100 MiB on phones, iPhone and iPad; everything else goes through hash-wasm HMAC Offered for MD5, SHA-1, the SHA-2 and SHA3 variants, BLAKE2b-512 and RIPEMD-160; the others are skipped while a key is set

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: Hashing runs in Web Workers inside your browser tab: your files and text are not sent to us, and the HMAC key stays in the page. If you turn on a translation in the language menu, Google receives the page's visible text, which includes the hash values shown. When the red box shows an error (a cancel excepted), we receive that error, the tool's name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Which hash should I use: MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256?
faq.a: Use the one the publisher lists, since a checksum can only be compared with the same algorithm. For new uses pick SHA-256: practical collisions are known for MD5 and SHA-1, not for SHA-256. MD5 and CRC32 still catch accidental corruption of a copy.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: No. The tool sets no cap: files are read in 8 MiB pieces by background workers. Files up to 700 MiB (100 MiB on phones, iPhone and iPad) are also loaded whole once, so SHA-1 and SHA-256/384/512 can use the faster Web Crypto. Speed depends on your device.

faq.q: How do I verify a downloaded file?
faq.a: Choose "Files", add the file, and paste the publisher's checksum, in hex or Base64, into "Expected hash, to verify (optional)". After hashing, the matching algorithm turns green if it is ticked; if none matches, the tool names the algorithms that give a hash of that length.

faq.q: Can sha256sum -c check the checksums.txt file?
faq.a: Yes for its SHA256 lines, and md5sum -c reads the MD5 lines. Each command checks only its own algorithm, so lines for CRC32, xxHash, BLAKE3, Keccak-256 or an HMAC are for reading. Tick only SHA-256 to get a file that sha256sum -c reads completely.

faq.q: What does the HMAC key do?
faq.a: With a key, each eligible algorithm computes an HMAC, such as HMAC-SHA256, the keyed hash used to sign API requests and webhooks. Keccak-256, BLAKE3, CRC32, CRC32C and the xxHash family are not offered with a key and are skipped until you clear it.

faq.q: Why does my text give a different hash elsewhere?
faq.a: A hidden difference in the bytes is the usual cause: the box hashes exactly its UTF-8 text, so a trailing newline, Windows line endings or another encoding elsewhere change the result. Compare the byte count shown above the results.

tips: Avoid MD5 and SHA-1 for anything security-sensitive — they are fine as checksums against accidental corruption, not against tampering. Use SHA-256 or better.
CRC32 and xxHash are checksums built for speed, not security: good for spotting corrupted copies, useless against deliberate changes.
Before hashing a large file, untick the algorithms you do not need: each one ticked adds work for the browser.

title: Hex to Text Converter — UTF-8 Bytes in Both Directions
desc: Decode hex bytes such as 48 65 6c or 0x48,0x65 into UTF-8 text, or turn text into hex bytes. Odd digit counts and non-text bytes are flagged.
ui: Hex to Text Convert between text and hexadecimal Text to Hex Hex to Text

about.heading: About Hex to Text
about.text: Hex to Text converts between text and its UTF-8 bytes written in hexadecimal, using your browser's own text encoder. Text to Hex writes each byte as two lowercase digits separated by spaces, so é gives c3 a9, ☕ three bytes and 😀 four. Hex to Text reads digit pairs with or without separators (spaces, commas, colons, semicolons, hyphens) and accepts the 0x48 and \x48 notations. It refuses an odd number of digits, characters that are not hex, and bytes that are not valid UTF-8, instead of printing garbage. Latin-1, UTF-16 and other encodings are not decoded.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A short text with an accent and an emoji turned into bytes, then C-style hex bytes turned back into text: Input Hi é😀 0x48,0x69,0x20,0xc3,0xa9 Result Text to Hex: 48 69 20 c3 a9 f0 9f 98 80 Hex to Text: Hi é

howto: Paste hex bytes, or the text you want to see as hex.
Click "Hex to Text" to decode the bytes as UTF-8, or "Text to Hex" to get space-separated byte pairs.
If the result box shows a message instead, it names the problem: an odd number of digits, a character that is not hex, or bytes that are not UTF-8.
Take the bytes or the text with "Copy", or save them in converted.txt through "Download".
howtoHeading: How to convert hex to text

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Hex input Pairs of 0-9 and a-f in either case; spaces, commas, colons, semicolons and hyphens ignored; 0x48 and \x48 forms accepted Hex output Lowercase byte pairs separated by single spaces Text encoding UTF-8 only, in both directions

Where your text is processed.heading: Where your text is processed
Where your text is processed.text: Both directions use your browser's TextEncoder and TextDecoder inside this page, so neither the hex nor the text leaves your computer. When the tool shows an error, such as an odd number of digits, or the browser refuses a copy, we receive that message, the tool's name and your browser's name and version, without what you pasted.

faq.q: Is é written as two bytes?
faq.a: Yes: c3 a9, because the tool writes UTF-8 bytes. e9 is the Latin-1 code for é; pasting e9 alone into Hex to Text gives an error, since that single byte is not valid UTF-8.

faq.q: What hex formats can I paste?
faq.a: Any pairs of hex digits: 48656c6c6f, 48 65 6c 6c 6f, 48:65:6c, 0x48,0x65 or \x48\x65. Upper and lower case both work, and separators are removed before decoding, so mixing them is fine.

faq.q: Can it decode Latin-1 or Windows-1252 bytes?
faq.a: No. The tool decodes UTF-8 only. Bytes saved in another encoding, or binary data, get the message that they are not valid UTF-8 text, rather than wrong characters.

faq.q: How many bytes does one character take?
faq.a: One to four in UTF-8: plain Latin letters one, most accented Latin letters two, ☕ and most Chinese and Japanese characters three, and emoji such as 😀 four (f0 9f 98 80).

tips: To see the \uXXXX escapes a JavaScript string uses instead of bytes, try Unicode Converter.

title: HTML Encoder — Escape & < > and Quotes as Entities
desc: Escape &, <, >, quotes and apostrophes before you put text into HTML, or decode entities back in one pass. Runs in your browser, nothing saved.
ui: HTML Encoder Encode and decode HTML entities Encode Decode

about.heading: About HTML Encoder
about.text: HTML Encoder escapes the five characters that HTML reads as markup: & becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, the double quote becomes " and the apostrophe becomes '. Use it before you put user text, a code sample or an attribute value into a page, so that it shows as text instead of being read as tags. All other characters, accents and emoji included, are left as they are. The Decode button does the reverse for named and numeric entities, in a single pass. Both buttons are handled by this page's own script.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A link with a quoted title and a comparison, escaped with Encode: Text 5 > 3 & 2 < 4 Encode <a title="Tom's">5 > 3 & 2 < 4</a>

howto: Paste the text or code sample you want to show on a web page.
Click "Encode" to replace the ampersand, the angle brackets and both kinds of quotes with entities.
To undo it, paste escaped text and click "Decode".
Click "Copy" and paste the escaped result into your HTML, or keep it with "Download" (the file is encoded.txt, even after a decode).
howtoHeading: How to escape text for HTML

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Escaped by Encode & < > and both quote marks, written & < > " ' Read by Decode Every named entity your browser knows, plus decimal and hex numeric entities Passes One: &lt; becomes <, never <

Where your text is processed.heading: Where your text is processed
Where your text is processed.text: Escaping is a plain text replacement done by this page's script, and named entities are looked up with your browser's own HTML parser, which runs no script and loads nothing. Nothing you paste leaves the page or is stored. When something fails, such as a copy the browser refuses, we get that error with the tool's name and your browser's name and version, not your text.

faq.q: Is escaping these five characters enough to make text safe in HTML?
faq.a: Yes for text between tags and for attribute values inside quotes. No for an unquoted attribute, a link address (a javascript: address stays harmful once escaped), or code placed inside script or style elements: those need other escaping or validation.

faq.q: Does Decode read both ' and '?
faq.a: Yes. Encode writes the apostrophe as ', and Decode turns both ' and ' back into an apostrophe, so text escaped either way reads the same after decoding.

faq.q: Does it encode accented letters or emoji?
faq.a: No. Only the five markup characters are replaced; é, ü or 😀 stay as they are, which suits any page saved as UTF-8. Decode still reads entities such as é or 😀 if you paste them.

faq.q: Will Encode then Decode give my text back?
faq.a: Yes. Decode reads each entity once, so the & written by Encode turns back into & without touching what follows it, and text that already contained entities comes back unchanged.

tips: Escape a code sample once only: encoding it twice makes the page show &lt; instead of <.

title: HTML Entity Decoder — &,  , € to Characters
desc: Turn &,  , é or 😀 into real characters without stripping tags. Useful for feed, CMS or e-mail source text.
ui: HTML Entity Decoder Turn HTML entities back into readable characters Encode Decode

about.heading: About HTML Entity Decoder
about.text: HTML Entity Decoder reads text full of HTML entities, as found in RSS feeds, CMS exports, scraped pages or e-mail source, and writes the real characters. Named entities such as é, — or   are looked up by your browser's HTML parser, so every name it knows works; numeric ones, decimal (€) or hex (€), are converted directly. Tags such as <b> are kept exactly, and each entity is decoded once per click. An Encode button is there too, for the opposite direction; both work inside this tab.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A line copied from a feed's source, decoded with one click: Text with entities Price: €5 – © 2026 😀 <b> Decode Price: €5 – © 2026 😀 <b>

howto: Paste the text that shows codes such as & or ' instead of characters.
Click "Decode" to replace every entity with its character; tags stay in place.
If the result still shows codes like <, the source was escaped twice: copy the result back into the input box and click "Decode" again.
The clean text lands in the lower box, where "Copy" takes it and "Download" saves it as decoded.txt.
howtoHeading: How to decode HTML entities

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Named entities Every name known to your browser's HTML parser, written with its final semicolon (a few old names also work without it) Numeric entities Decimal and hex, up to U+10FFFF; zero, surrogates and larger codes give the replacement character Tags and other text Left exactly as written

Where your text is processed.heading: Where your text is processed
Where your text is processed.text: Decoding happens in this tab: numeric codes are converted by the page's own script, and each named entity is handed alone to your browser's DOMParser, which does not run scripts or fetch images. What you paste stays in this tab and disappears when it closes. A crash of this page, a blocked clipboard included, sends us an error report with the cleaned error message, this tool's name and your browser with its version; nothing you pasted is part of it.

faq.q: Why does my text still show & after decoding?
faq.a: It was escaped twice, which some CMS and export scripts do: &amp; decodes to &. Each Decode removes exactly one layer and always reads the input box, so copy the result back into it and decode again to reach the plain character.

faq.q: Are HTML tags removed?
faq.a:
No. Only entities change; tags such as ,

or stay exactly as written in the output. That keeps the markup intact when you only want readable accents and symbols.

faq.q: Is   turned into an ordinary space?
faq.a: No. It becomes a non-breaking space (U+00A0), which looks the same on screen but is a different character, so a search or a comparison with a normal space will not match it.

faq.q: Which numeric entities give a replacement character?
faq.a: Zero, the surrogate range � to � and anything above  give �. Codes 128 to 159 give invisible control characters here, whereas browsers display them as Windows-1252 symbols such as an en dash.

tips: Paste the page source, not the rendered page: text copied from a displayed page has no entities left to decode.
Need the reverse? "Encode" on this page escapes the ampersand, angle brackets and quotes.

title: JavaScript Formatter & Minifier — Beautify or Shrink JS

about.heading: About JavaScript Formatter
about.text: JavaScript Formatter does two opposite jobs on the same code. Format uses js-beautify: 2-space indentation, one statement per line, spaces around operators, at most one blank line kept in a row, and strings, template literals, regular expressions and comments left as written. Minify uses Terser, the same engine as JS Minifier: it parses the code, shortens local names and removes dead code and comments. Format never complains about invalid code; Minify stops and shows Terser's message, without a line number. js-beautify and Terser both work on your code inside the browser tab.

Where your code is processed.heading: Where your code is processed
Where your code is processed.text: The formatter and the minifier are JavaScript libraries loaded into this page on first use; they read your code inside the browser, and your code is not uploaded. When a Minify error appears, its message is sent to our error log with quoted text, long numbers and addresses replaced, along with the tool name and the name and version of your browser.

faq.q: Does formatting change what my code does?
faq.a: No. Format only changes whitespace: indentation, line breaks and spaces around operators and keywords. Strings, template literals, regular expressions and comments are kept exactly as written.

faq.q: Is minified code safe to use?
faq.a: Yes, when Terser accepts it: it parses the code first, so automatic semicolon insertion and expressions such as a - -b keep their meaning. Global names stay; only names local to a function are shortened.

faq.q: Does the Minify error give a line number?
faq.a: No. The page shows only Terser's message, such as Name expected, and not the position Terser keeps separately. To locate the error, paste the code into Code Formatter, which reports syntax errors with line and column.

tips: Format minified code from a website to read it; keep your own readable source and minify a copy for deployment.

about.heading: About JS Minifier
about.text: JS Minifier compresses JavaScript with Terser in your browser. Terser parses the code first, so the result behaves like the original: code written without semicolons, a return followed by a line break, regular expressions and expressions such as a - -b are handled. Names local to functions are shortened, global names and object properties are kept, unreachable code such as an if (false) block is removed, and every comment is dropped. Modern syntax is accepted, including classes, async functions, optional chaining and BigInt, and so are import and export lines. TypeScript is not: convert it first.

example.heading: Example
example.text: No semicolons in the input; Terser adds them, puts everything on one line and renames the locals. Input function total(prices) { let sum = 0 for (const price of prices) sum += price return sum } console.log(total([1, 2])) Minified Output function total(o){let t=0;for(const l of o)t+=l;return t}console.log(total([1,2]));

howto: Paste your script into "Input".
Click "Minify".
Read "Minified Output" and the characters-saved line; if the code does not parse, Error: and Terser's message appear instead.
Click "Copy", or "Download" to keep "minified.js".
howtoHeading: How to minify JavaScript

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JavaScript, scripts or ES modules Output Minified JavaScript on one line, saved as minified.js Settings Compress and mangle on, comments off, top-level names kept Errors Terser's message, without line or column

Where your script is processed.heading: Where your script is processed
Where your script is processed.text: Terser is downloaded once, on your first click on "Minify", and then works on your device: the script is not uploaded. A failed minification is the exception, since the error message shown, with quoted strings, long numbers and addresses replaced, is reported to our error log with the tool's name and your browser's name and version; an unexpected failure of the page is reported the same way.

faq.q: Will minified code behave the same?
faq.a: Yes. Terser only applies transformations that keep the behavior of code it could parse, including code written without semicolons; a return followed by a line break still returns nothing, as in the original.

faq.q: Does it rename variables?
faq.a: Yes, but only local ones: variables and parameters inside functions get one-letter names, as total(prices) becoming total(o) in the example. Top-level names and object properties are kept, so other scripts can still call them.

faq.q: Can it minify TypeScript?
faq.a: No. Type annotations are a syntax error for Terser. Use Code Minifier in TS mode, which removes the types and minifies in one step, or run TypeScript to JavaScript first and paste its output here.

faq.q: Does it show where a syntax error is?
faq.a: No. Only Terser's message is shown, for example Name expected, without its line and column. Paste the code into Code Formatter to see the position of the first syntax error.

about.heading: About JSON Formatter
about.text: JSON Formatter checks your JSON with the browser's JSON.parse, then re-indents the text you pasted instead of rebuilding it from parsed values. That is why 20-digit ids and 1.10 stay exactly as written, and so do escapes unless you sort the keys. Choose 2 spaces, 4 spaces or a tab, tick Sort keys A-Z to order the keys of every object at every depth, or use Minify for a single line. Invalid JSON is reported with its line and column, and the faulty line is shown with a caret under the problem. There is no tree view and no syntax coloring. Validation and re-indenting run in your browser.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Format with 2 spaces: the 20-digit id and 1.10 are copied, not recalculated. Input {"id":12345678901234567890,"price":1.10,"tags":["a","b"],"meta":{}} Output { "id": 12345678901234567890, "price": 1.10, "tags": [ "a", "b" ], "meta": {} }

howto: Paste JSON into "Input".
Choose "2 spaces", "4 spaces" or "Tab" under Indent, and tick "Sort keys A-Z" if you want ordered keys.
Click "Format", or "Minify" for a single line.
If the JSON is invalid, read the red line under the boxes: it gives the line and column, and the block below marks the spot with ^.

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text, pasted Output Indented or one-line JSON, saved as formatted.json Indent 2 spaces, 4 spaces or a tab Sort keys A-Z Every object at every depth, by character code (capitals first); numbers kept, strings re-escaped Length The code sets no maximum; above 1,000,000 characters the boxes show only the first 20,000 characters

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: JSON.parse and the re-indenter are part of the page, so formatting and validation take place in your browser and your JSON is not uploaded. If an Invalid JSON message is displayed, that message, with the quoted part of your JSON, long numbers and addresses removed, is reported to our error log, together with the tool name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Does it show where my JSON is invalid?
faq.a: Yes. Click "Format" and the message gives the line and column of the first error, while the box below shows that line with a caret under the problem. Trailing commas, single quotes and unquoted keys are the usual causes.

faq.q: Will formatting change my numbers?
faq.a: No. The output is built from your original text, so 12345678901234567890 and 1.10 are copied as typed, whereas re-serializing would print 12345678901234567000 and 1.1. With Sort keys A-Z, numbers stay exact but escapes such as \u00e9 are rewritten as the character.

faq.q: Does Sort keys A-Z ignore case?
faq.a: No. Keys are ordered by character code at every depth, so capitals come first: B sorts before a. If a key appears twice in one object, only its last value is kept. Arrays keep their original order.

faq.q: Is there a tree view?
faq.a: No. The output is plain text in a box, with no collapsible tree and no colors. The indentation, and the caret shown for an error, are the only guides.

tips: A JSON file that starts with a byte order mark is rejected here as invalid; JSON Minifier and Code Formatter remove that mark first.

It validates the text with the browser's JSON.parse first, then copies your original characters, so values are never re-serialized: a 20-digit id, 1.10, 1e21 and escapes stay exactly as written, and spaces inside strings are kept. A byte order mark at the start is removed. The line under the result gives the characters saved and the percentage. The page has no option to sort keys or change values, and it does its work in your browser.
