Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: Minification is a few lines of JavaScript in this page: your JSON is read and rewritten in the browser and never uploaded. When the page displays an error, Invalid JSON followed by the browser's reason, that message is reported to our error log with the tool name and your browser's name and version, cleaned of quoted passages, long numbers and addresses.

faq.q: Will minifying change my data?
faq.a: No. Only whitespace outside strings is removed. Keys, values, numbers and escapes are copied character for character, so large ids are not rounded, and two spaces inside a string value stay two spaces.

faq.q: Does it tell me when the JSON is invalid?
faq.a: Yes. A red Invalid JSON message with the browser's explanation appears and nothing new is produced. A result from an earlier run stays in the output box, so read the message before copying.

faq.q: Does it also sort or clean my JSON?
faq.a: No. It keeps key order, duplicate keys and values as they are. To sort keys or pick an indentation, use JSON Formatter, which offers sorting and three indent choices.

title: JSON to C# Class Generator — System.Text.Json Ready
desc: Make C# classes from JSON: PascalCase properties, [JsonPropertyName] attributes, long, double and nullable types, built by quicktype in your browser.
ui: JSON to C# Class Generate C# classes from JSON JSON Input C# Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to C# Class
about.text: JSON to C# Class writes C# model classes from a JSON sample with quicktype-core, inside your browser. The code sits in namespace App with the System.Text.Json usings; each nested object gets a public partial class, properties are PascalCase, and a [JsonPropertyName] attribute keeps every original key. Whole numbers are long, decimals double, and arrays become arrays such as Item[]. Properties missing from some array elements are nullable and carry a [JsonIgnore] attribute for null values. It targets System.Text.Json only, with no Newtonsoft attributes and no records. A value with two types, such as a number in one item and text in another, adds a union struct and the JsonConverter classes it needs.

example.heading: Example
example.text: An order with line items; note appears in only one item, so it becomes nullable. JSON Input {"orderId": 1001, "total": 49.90, "paid": true, "items": [{"sku": "A1", "qty": 2}, {"sku": "B7", "qty": 1, "note": "gift"}]} C# Output namespace App { using System; using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Text.Json; using System.Text.Json.Serialization; using System.Globalization; public partial class Root { [JsonPropertyName("orderId")] public long OrderId { get; set; } [JsonPropertyName("total")] public double Total { get; set; } [JsonPropertyName("paid")] public bool Paid { get; set; } [JsonPropertyName("items")] public Item[] Items { get; set; } } public partial class Item { [JsonPropertyName("sku")] public string Sku { get; set; } [JsonPropertyName("qty")] public long Qty { get; set; } [JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)] [JsonPropertyName("note")] public string? Note { get; set; } } }

howto: Paste a JSON sample into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert" to get the classes in "C# Output".
Replace the namespace App line with the namespace of your project.
Click "Copy" or "Download" to keep the code as "Model.cs".
howtoHeading: How to generate C# classes from JSON

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON object or array of objects, as text Output C# classes in namespace App, saved as Model.cs Serializer System.Text.Json: [JsonPropertyName] on every property, [JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)] on optional ones Types long, double, bool, string and arrays (T[]); object for a key that is null in every sample; a union struct when a value has two types

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: Classes are generated by JavaScript running on your own device; the JSON you paste and the C# you get are never uploaded. The quicktype library loads when you first press Convert. When the page displays an error, our error log receives its text, cleaned of quoted fragments, long numbers and web or e-mail addresses, with the tool's name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Does it work with Newtonsoft.Json (Json.NET)?
faq.a: No. The generated attributes belong to System.Text.Json: [JsonPropertyName] for names and [JsonIgnore] for optional values. To use the classes with Newtonsoft.Json, replace them with its own [JsonProperty] attribute by hand.

faq.q: Will the classes deserialize my JSON as they are?
faq.a: Yes, when every key keeps one type: JsonSerializer.Deserialize maps each property to its original key through [JsonPropertyName]. When a value mixes types, pass Converter.Settings, which the output then contains, as the second argument. The types come only from your sample, so check them against more data.

faq.q: Is a property typed object when its value is always null?
faq.a: Yes. When a key is null in every element of your sample, no type can be inferred, so it becomes object. Paste an example where the key holds a real value, or set the type yourself, for example string? for an optional text.

faq.q: Can I use int instead of long?
faq.a: Yes. Whole numbers are always typed long so that large values fit; if your values are small, change long to int by hand, and the attribute and the key mapping keep working.

tips: Paste an array with several items so that properties which are sometimes absent become nullable.

title: JSON to CSV Converter — Nested Objects to Dotted Columns
desc: Paste a JSON array or object and get CSV: nested objects become columns like address.city, arrays like tags.0. Large numbers keep every digit.
ui: JSON to CSV Convert JSON to CSV format JSON Input CSV Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to CSV
about.text: JSON to CSV turns pasted JSON into comma-separated text with a header row. It takes an array of objects, a single object (one row) or an array of plain values (one value column). Every key seen in any object becomes a column, in first-seen order (keys that are whole numbers, such as 10, come first); nested objects are flattened to dotted names and arrays to numbered ones. Numbers are copied exactly as written, so a 20-digit ID is not rounded. Values with a comma, a quote, a line break or spaces at either end are quoted. The JSON is read and the CSV written inside your browser tab.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Two objects with different keys, a nested address and a tags array, and the CSV the tool returns: JSON [ {"id": 12345678901234567890, "name": "Ann", "address": {"city": "Paris"}, "tags": ["a", "b"]}, {"id": 2, "name": "Lee, Bo", "email": null} ] CSV id,name,address.city,tags.0,tags.1,email 12345678901234567890,Ann,Paris,a,b, 2,"Lee, Bo",,,,

howto: Paste your JSON into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert".
Check the header row and the columns in "CSV Output".
Take the result with "Copy", or keep it as data.csv with "Download".
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to CSV

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text: an array of objects, one object, or an array of values Output comma-separated text with a header row, saved as data.csv Missing keys and null empty cell

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: The JSON is parsed and the CSV built in your browser when you click "Convert"; the text you paste is not uploaded. If an error occurs, such as invalid JSON, we receive its message with quoted text masked, plus the tool name and your browser and version.

faq.q: Can it flatten nested JSON?
faq.a: Yes. An address object with a city key becomes the column address.city, and a tags array becomes tags.0, tags.1 and so on, at any depth. An empty object or array is written as {} or [] so its column is not lost.

faq.q: Is it a problem if objects have different keys?
faq.a: No. The columns are the union of all keys, in the order they first appear (whole-number keys first), and a row without a key gets an empty cell there. A null value also gives an empty cell, and true and false are written as words.

faq.q: Can I convert a single JSON string or number?
faq.a: No. The top level must be an array or an object; otherwise the tool answers that the JSON must be an array of objects, or a single object. An empty array is refused too, since it has no row to write.

faq.q: Can I choose another separator than the comma?
faq.a: No. The output always uses commas, with the header first and one row per line; a value holding a line break stays quoted over several lines. If you need tabs instead, copy the result and paste it into CSV to TSV, which detects the comma and writes tab-separated text.

tips: To build JSON from a CSV file, use CSV to JSON, which can also type numeric columns.

title: JSON to Go Struct Generator — json Tags and Pointers
desc: Turn a JSON sample into Go structs with json tags, int64 or float64 fields and pointers for optional keys. Built in your browser with quicktype.
ui: JSON to Go Struct Generate Go structs from JSON JSON Input Go Struct Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to Go Struct
about.text: JSON to Go Struct turns a JSON sample into Go type declarations for encoding/json, generated by quicktype-core in your browser. Each nested object becomes its own named struct, field names follow Go style including initialisms (user_id becomes UserID), and every field keeps the original key in a json tag. Whole numbers are int64 and numbers written with a decimal point are float64. When you paste an array, a key that only some elements have becomes a pointer with omitempty. The output holds only the type definitions: no package line, no methods, no marshal helpers.

example.heading: Example
example.text: One object with a nested address: the address gets its own struct. JSON Input {"user_id": 42, "score": 9.5, "tags": ["go", "api"], "address": {"city": "Montreal", "zip": "H2X"}} Go Struct Output type Root struct { UserID int64 `json:"user_id"` Score float64 `json:"score"` Tags []string `json:"tags"` Address Address `json:"address"` } type Address struct { City string `json:"city"` Zip string `json:"zip"` }

howto: Paste the JSON, for example an API response, into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert" to build the structs in "Go Struct Output".
Add your own package line above the types, since the tool writes only the declarations.
Click "Copy", or "Download" to get the file "model.go".
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to a Go struct

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text; with an array, the fields of all elements are merged Output Go struct declarations with json tags, saved as model.go Number types int64 for whole numbers; float64 for numbers written with a point or an exponent, such as 10.0 Optional keys Pointer type plus omitempty when a key is missing from some elements; pointer alone when it is null in some; interface{} when it is null in every sample Mixed types A key that holds a number in one element and text in another becomes a struct with Integer and String pointer fields; encoding/json cannot fill it without an UnmarshalJSON method you write

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: Struct generation runs in this browser tab. The quicktype engine is fetched once, on your first click, and your JSON stays on your computer. The page does send error reports: when a red error line appears, its wording, with quoted parts, long numbers and addresses stripped, goes to our error log along with the tool name and the name and version of your browser, and an unexpected failure of the page is reported the same way.

faq.q: Is a field a pointer when a key is sometimes missing or null?
faq.a: Yes. A key missing from at least one element becomes a pointer with omitempty, which leaves it out when encoding; a key that is null in one element becomes a plain pointer, without omitempty. If the key is always set in your real data, change *string to string by hand.

faq.q: Which number types does it use?
faq.a: int64 for whole numbers and float64 for decimals. A value written as 10.0 counts as a decimal, so it becomes float64 and a later 10.5 still decodes. Switch to int or int32 yourself if your values are small.

faq.q: How does it name fields from snake_case keys?
faq.a: It turns them into exported Go names and keeps the key in the tag: user_id becomes UserID, and its tag still says user_id, so encoding/json reads and writes the original key unchanged.

faq.q: Can it generate a struct for a JSON array?
faq.a: Yes. A top-level array gives type Root []RootElement, and the fields of all elements are merged into RootElement, so one element without a key is enough to mark that key optional.

tips: Paste two or three different items from an API list rather than one, so that keys that are sometimes absent become pointers.

title: JSON to PHP Array or Class Converter — PHP 8 Classes
desc: Convert JSON to a PHP array literal with your exact values, or to typed PHP 8 classes with a fromArray() factory, written by our own code in your browser.
ui: JSON to PHP Class Turn JSON into a PHP array or typed PHP 8 classes JSON Input PHP Output PHP array (the data, as json_decode($json, true) returns it) PHP classes (typed, PHP 8+) Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to PHP Class
about.text: JSON to PHP Class turns JSON into PHP code in two ways. PHP array, selected by default, writes your data as a $data = [ ... ]; literal in short array syntax, matching what json_decode($json, true) returns: strings escaped, numbers as written (1.10 stays 1.10), integers above PHP_INT_MAX kept as strings. PHP classes writes final PHP 8 classes, one per nested object, with typed promoted properties, nullable types for keys that are missing or sometimes null, and a fromArray() factory that reads the original keys. This page does not use quicktype: the converter is the site's own code, run in your browser.

example.heading: Example
example.text: PHP array output; the id is larger than PHP_INT_MAX, so it is kept as a string. JSON Input {"name": "Ada", "roles": ["admin", "dev"], "price": 1.10, "id": 12345678901234567890} PHP Output <?php // Integers beyond PHP_INT_MAX are written as strings, as json_decode() does with JSON_BIGINT_AS_STRING; as a float they would lose digits. $data = [ 'name' => 'Ada', 'roles' => [ 'admin', 'dev', ], 'price' => 1.10, 'id' => '12345678901234567890', ];

howto: Paste the JSON object or array you want as PHP into "JSON Input".
Keep "PHP array" to get your values, or pick "PHP classes" to get typed classes.
Click "Convert" to fill "PHP Output".
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save it as "data.php".
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to a PHP array or class

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Output modes PHP array (default) or PHP classes Input JSON text; class mode needs an object or an array of objects PHP version Array: 5.4 or later. Classes: 8.0 or later (constructor promotion, named arguments, mixed) Large integers PHP array: values above PHP_INT_MAX are written as strings, with a comment. PHP classes: typed string, no comment; the json_decode call shown in the Usage line needs JSON_BIGINT_AS_STRING to keep the digits

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: This converter is plain JavaScript executed by your browser, with no library to download, and the JSON never leaves your computer. If a message such as Invalid JSON or the class-mode warning is displayed, that message, stripped of quoted text, long numbers and addresses, is reported to our error log, along with the tool's name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Can I get a PHP array with my actual data?
faq.a: Yes. Keep "PHP array" selected: the output is $data = [ 'key' => value, ... ]; with nested arrays for nested objects. For a config file that must return an array, replace $data = with return.

faq.q: Which PHP version do the classes need?
faq.a: 8.0 or later. They use constructor property promotion, named arguments in fromArray() and the mixed type, all introduced in PHP 8.0. The array output only needs short array syntax, available since PHP 5.4.

faq.q: What happens to very large integers?
faq.a: In the PHP array output they become strings: a JSON integer above PHP_INT_MAX would lose digits as a PHP float, so it is written in quotes, as json_decode does with JSON_BIGINT_AS_STRING, and a comment says so. In class mode the property is typed string with no comment; decode with JSON_BIGINT_AS_STRING to keep the digits.

faq.q: Can class mode convert a list of numbers?
faq.a: No. Classes need an object or an array of objects. For a list of numbers or strings, or a single value, the page shows a message asking you to use the array output instead.

tips: In class mode, paste several array elements: keys present in only some of them become nullable properties.
Keys such as first-name become camelCase properties (firstName), while fromArray() still reads the original key.

title: JSON to Python Dataclass Generator — Typed, snake_case
desc: Turn JSON into Python @dataclass definitions with int, float, str, List, Optional and Union types and snake_case names, made by quicktype on your device.
ui: JSON to Python Class Generate Python dataclasses from JSON JSON Input Python Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to Python Class
about.text: JSON to Python Class generates Python 3.7+ dataclasses that describe the shape of a JSON sample: type definitions, not a dict holding your values. It runs quicktype-core in your browser. Each nested object becomes a @dataclass, field names are converted to snake_case (first-name becomes first_name), and types use int, float, str, bool, List and Optional from typing, plus Union when a value has two types and Any for an empty array. Fields absent from some array elements get Optional[...] = None and are placed after the required ones, as dataclasses require. There is no from_dict or to_dict helper: you create the objects yourself.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Two people; only Ada has a spouse, so spouse becomes Optional. JSON Input [{"first-name": "Ada", "age": 36, "spouse": {"name": "Bob"}}, {"first-name": "Lin", "age": 29}] Python Output from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Optional @dataclass class Spouse: name: str @dataclass class RootElement: first_name: str age: int spouse: Optional[Spouse] = None

howto: Paste your JSON into "JSON Input"; an array of several records gives better types than a single one.
Click "Convert" to see the dataclasses in "Python Output".
Check renamed fields: keys that clash with Python keywords get a prefix, such as root_class for class.
Click "Copy", or "Download" for a "model.py" file.
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to Python dataclasses

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON object, or array of objects; an array of plain values such as [1, 2] gives an empty output Output Python dataclasses with typing annotations, saved as model.py Names snake_case fields; a top-level array gives a class named RootElement Python version 3.7 or later (dataclasses module)

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: The dataclasses are produced locally, in your browser, by the quicktype engine that loads on your first conversion; your JSON is not transmitted to us. If the tool displays an error, the message text is reported to our error log with the tool's name and your browser and its version, after quoted parts, long numbers and addresses are stripped from it.

faq.q: Does it create a dict with my data?
faq.a: No. It writes dataclass definitions that describe the data. To get a dict with your values, use json.loads on the text; to fill a dataclass, pass the matching values to its constructor.

faq.q: How are optional and null fields typed?
faq.a: Optional[T] = None, when a key is missing from some array elements or null in some of them. A key that is null in every element has nothing to infer from and is typed None, so give it a real value in the sample if you want a type.

faq.q: Does it generate Pydantic models?
faq.a: No. The output uses the standard dataclasses module only. Because the annotations are ordinary typing hints, you can turn a class into a Pydantic model by replacing @dataclass with a BaseModel subclass.

faq.q: Are whole numbers and decimals kept apart?
faq.a: Yes. Whole numbers are typed int, and numbers written with a decimal point or an exponent are typed float, even 10.0, so a later value such as 10.5 still matches the annotation.

tips: Rename RootElement or Root to a name that describes your records before you use the classes.

title: JSON to Rust Struct Generator — serde Derive Ready
desc: Paste JSON to get Rust structs that derive Serialize and Deserialize, with snake_case fields, serde renames and Option for missing keys. In-browser.
ui: JSON to Rust Struct Generate Rust structs from JSON JSON Input Rust Struct Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to Rust Struct
about.text: JSON to Rust Struct generates structs for serde from a JSON sample, with quicktype-core running in your browser. Every struct derives Debug, Clone, Serialize and Deserialize. Fields are snake_case, and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] or #[serde(rename = "...")] keeps the JSON keys, so serde_json reads and writes them unchanged. Whole numbers are i64, decimals f64, arrays Vec, and a key missing from some elements is an Option with skip_serializing_if, so None is not written back. A top-level array also gets a type alias such as pub type Root = Vec<RootElement>.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Only the first user has a bio, so bio becomes an Option. JSON Input [{"userName": "ada", "followers": 120, "bio": "Hi"}, {"userName": "lin", "followers": 3}] Rust Struct Output use serde::{Serialize, Deserialize}; pub type Root = Vec<RootElement>; #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct RootElement { pub user_name: String, pub followers: i64, #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub bio: Option<String>, }

howto: Paste a JSON sample, ideally an array of several records, into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert"; the structs appear in "Rust Struct Output".
Add serde with the derive feature, and serde_json, to your Cargo.toml.
Click "Copy" or "Download" ("model.rs") to put the code in your crate.
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to Rust structs

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text; arrays are merged element by element Output Rust structs with derives and serde attributes, saved as model.rs Types i64, f64, bool, String, Vec<T> and Option<T>; an untagged enum when a value has two types; serde_json::Value when no type can be inferred (a key that is always null, an empty array) Dependencies serde with the derive feature; serde_json to parse, also named in the code for a key that is null in every sample

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: Quicktype is downloaded at the first conversion and turns your JSON into Rust inside the browser tab, without uploading the sample. When the page shows an error, the error text is reported to our error log, together with the tool name and your browser's name and version, after quoted fragments, long numbers and addresses are removed.

faq.q: How are camelCase or hyphenated keys handled?
faq.a: Fields are renamed to snake_case. When all keys of a struct follow camelCase, one #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] covers it; other keys get their own #[serde(rename = "...")]. serde_json therefore reads and writes the original keys.

faq.q: Does a key missing from some items become an Option?
faq.a: Yes, and so does a key that is null in some items. Each gets a skip_serializing_if attribute set to Option::is_none, so a field holding None is left out when you serialize, as it was absent in the original JSON.

faq.q: Which integer type does it use?
faq.a: i64 for whole numbers, and f64 for any number written with a decimal point or an exponent, including 10.0. Change i64 to u32 or another type by hand if you know the range of your values.

faq.q: Which crates does the generated code need?
faq.a: Two at most: serde with the derive feature, for the derives and rename attributes, and serde_json, which you need to parse JSON anyway and which the code names directly when a key is null in every sample.

tips: Rename RootElement and Root after pasting; those names come from the tool, not from your JSON.

title: JSON to TOML Converter — Tables and Arrays of Tables
desc: Paste a JSON object and get TOML: nested objects become [tables], arrays of objects [[tables]], null keys are left out and big integers kept.
ui: JSON to TOML Convert JSON to TOML format JSON Input TOML Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to TOML
about.text: JSON to TOML writes a pasted JSON object as a TOML file, the format of Cargo.toml and pyproject.toml. Nested objects become [section] tables, arrays of objects become [[section]] arrays of tables, and other arrays stay inline. Strings, numbers and booleans keep their types; a date written as a JSON string stays a quoted string. TOML has no null, so a null value on a key is left out and a null inside an array stops the conversion. Integers beyond the TOML range are written as quoted text with a notice. smol-toml writes the TOML inside your browser tab.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A JSON object with a date string, an ID too large for TOML, an array of objects and a null, and what the tool returns; the last line is the notice shown under the boxes, not part of the TOML: JSON { "title": "Demo", "released": "2024-01-15", "owner": {"name": "Ann", "id": 12345678901234567890}, "servers": [{"host": "a", "port": 8080}, {"host": "b", "port": 8081}], "note": null } TOML title = "Demo" released = "2024-01-15" [owner] name = "Ann" id = "12345678901234567890" [[servers]] host = "a" port = 8080 [[servers]] host = "b" port = 8081 Beyond what TOML numbers hold (integers up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, floats up to about 1.8e308): owner.id written as text (in quotes) to keep every digit.

howto: Paste a JSON object, not an array, into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert".
Read the TOML in "TOML Output" and any notice about numbers written as text.
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save data.toml.
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to TOML

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON object at the top level Output TOML text, file data.toml Integers up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807; larger ones become quoted text null left out on a key, refused inside an array

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: smol-toml writes the TOML in your browser; the JSON you paste is not uploaded, and the TOML stays on the page until you copy it or save data.toml. Error reports, whether or not a message is shown, carry the cleaned error text, the error type, the tool name and your browser name and version.

faq.q: Can TOML hold a JSON null?
faq.a: No. TOML has no null type, so a key whose value is null is simply left out. A null inside an array cannot be dropped without changing the array, so the tool stops with the message arrays cannot contain null or undefined values.

faq.q: Can I convert a JSON array?
faq.a: No, not at the top level: a TOML document is a table of keys, so the tool asks you to wrap the array in an object, for example under an items key. Arrays inside the object are converted normally.

faq.q: Are ISO date strings turned into TOML dates?
faq.a: No. JSON has no date type, so 2024-01-15 arrives as a string and is written in quotes, as the example shows. Remove the quotes by hand if you want a TOML date.

faq.q: Are very large numbers kept?
faq.a: Yes, digit for digit. An integer above 9,223,372,036,854,775,807, or a float beyond the range of a double, cannot be a TOML number, so it is written as quoted text and a notice names the key.

related: TOML to JSON — the other way.
JSON to YAML — the same object as YAML.
JSON Formatter — check your JSON is valid before converting.

title: JSON to TypeScript Interface Generator — Optional Fields
desc: Paste JSON and get TypeScript interfaces: one per nested object, ? for keys some items lack, | null for null values, written by quicktype on your device.
ui: JSON to TypeScript Generate TypeScript interfaces from JSON JSON Input TypeScript Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to TypeScript
about.text: JSON to TypeScript reads a JSON sample and writes the TypeScript interfaces that describe it, using the quicktype-core engine in your browser. Every nested object becomes its own exported interface, and every element of an array is examined: a key that some elements lack gets a question mark, and a value that is sometimes null is typed with null in a union. Keys that are not valid identifiers, such as first-name, are written in quotes. It generates types only: no classes, no runtime checks, and no enums, dates or UUID types guessed from string values.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Two array elements: nickname is null in one, team exists only in the second. JSON Input [{"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "nickname": null}, {"id": 2, "name": "Lin", "nickname": "lin", "team": {"name": "core", "size": 4}}] TypeScript Output export interface Root { id: number; name: string; nickname: null | string; team?: Team; } export interface Team { name: string; size: number; }

howto: Paste a JSON object, or an array of several representative objects, into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert"; the engine loads on the first click, then the interfaces fill "TypeScript Output".
Check the optional keys and the null unions against the data your code will really receive.
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save the code as "types.ts".
howtoHeading: How to generate TypeScript interfaces from JSON

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text: an object, or an array of objects whose elements are merged; an array of plain values gives an empty output Output Exported TypeScript interfaces, one per nested object, saved as types.ts Optional keys A question mark when a key is missing from some array elements; null in a union when a value is null Not generated Classes, runtime validation, enums, date or UUID types (strings stay string)

Where your JSON is processed.heading: Where your JSON is processed
Where your JSON is processed.text: The interfaces are generated in your browser: the page fetches the quicktype engine on your first click, and your JSON is not uploaded, nor is the TypeScript it produces. If an error message appears, a shortened copy of that message, with quoted text, long numbers and addresses removed, is sent to our error log together with the tool's name and your browser's name and version, so the tool can be fixed.

faq.q: Does it detect optional fields?
faq.a: Yes, when you paste an array. All elements are merged: a key missing from some of them is written with a question mark, and a key that is null in some of them gets null in its type, for example null | string. With a single object, every key it contains is required.

faq.q: How are nested objects and arrays typed?
faq.a: Each nested object becomes a separate exported interface named after its key, such as Team for a team key, and an array of objects becomes an array of that interface. Arrays of strings or numbers become string[] or number[].

faq.q: What happens to keys with hyphens or spaces?
faq.a: They keep their exact spelling as quoted property names, which is valid TypeScript, so the interface matches the JSON without any renaming. Keys that are valid identifiers, like nickname, are written without quotes.

faq.q: Can I save the result as a .ts file?
faq.a: Yes. After a conversion, a row named types.ts appears under the output with a "Download" button; on iPhone and iPad a "Save / Share" button is added next to it. "Copy" puts the same code on the clipboard.

tips: Rename the Root interface after pasting it into your project; the name comes from the tool, not from your data.
If the result is an Invalid JSON message, open the same text in JSON Formatter, which points to the line and column of the mistake.

title: JSON to XML Converter — Attributes, Arrays, Escaped Text
desc: Paste JSON and get indented XML under a root element. Arrays become repeated tags, @_ keys become attributes, and & or < are escaped. In your browser.
ui: JSON to XML Convert JSON to XML format JSON Input XML Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to XML
about.text: JSON to XML writes pasted JSON as an indented XML document that starts with an XML declaration and wraps everything in a root element. Each key becomes a tag; an array becomes the same tag repeated, and a top-level array becomes item elements. Keys that start with @_ become attributes and a #text key becomes the text of its element, following the fast-xml-parser conventions. Text is escaped, numbers are kept as written, and a key that cannot be an XML name is reported instead of producing broken XML.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A book object with an @_id key, an array and an ampersand, and the XML the tool returns: JSON { "book": { "@_id": "7", "title": "Tom & Jerry", "tags": ["kids", "cartoon"], "price": 12.50 } } XML <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <root> <book id="7"> <title>Tom & Jerry</title> <tags>kids</tags> <tags>cartoon</tags> <price>12.50</price> </book> </root>

howto: Paste JSON into "JSON Input"; put @_ before any key you want as an attribute.
Click "Convert".
Read the XML in "XML Output", or the message naming a key that is not a valid XML name.
Use "Copy", or "Download" for a data.xml file.
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to XML

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text Output XML with a declaration, a root element and two-space indentation; file data.xml Element names a letter or _ first, then letters, digits, _ . - or :

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: The XML is built in your browser by the fast-xml-parser library, loaded when you first click "Convert"; your JSON is not uploaded. When a conversion fails, a report reaches us with the error text, quoted parts masked, the tool name and your browser name and version.

faq.q: Can I create XML attributes?
faq.a: Yes. Prefix the key with @_: a book object holding @_id with the value 7 gives <book id="7">. A #text key next to it becomes the element's text, so one element can carry both attributes and content.

faq.q: Does the output have a single root element?
faq.a: Yes. An XML document needs exactly one, so the result is always wrapped in <root>; a JSON array at the top level gives one <item> per entry inside it. Rename root afterwards if your system expects another name.

faq.q: Are special characters escaped?
faq.a: Yes. & becomes & and < becomes < in text, as the example shows, so the document stays well-formed. A key with a space, or one that starts with a digit, is refused with a message, because no escaping can turn it into a valid tag name.

faq.q: Are numbers written exactly as in the JSON?
faq.a: Yes. The JSON is read without turning numbers into floating point, so a price of 12.50 gives <price>12.50</price> and a 20-digit ID keeps every digit in its element. A null value becomes an empty element.

tips: To read XML back into JSON, with attributes as @_ keys, use XML to JSON.

title: JSON to YAML Converter — Exact Numbers, Safe Quoting
desc: Paste JSON and get block-style YAML. Numbers stay as written, and strings such as yes, no or 1.10 are quoted so they stay text. In your browser.
ui: JSON to YAML Convert JSON to YAML format JSON Input YAML Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About JSON to YAML
about.text: JSON to YAML rewrites pasted JSON as YAML, the format of Kubernetes, Docker Compose and GitHub Actions files. Objects become indented mappings and arrays become lists of - items, at any depth; empty objects and arrays are written {} and []. Numbers are copied exactly as in the JSON, so 1.10 and a 20-digit ID are not changed. A string that a YAML reader could take for something else, such as yes, no, 123, a date or text containing a colon followed by a space, is put in single quotes. Long lines are never folded, and the work happens in your browser with js-yaml.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A small JSON configuration and the YAML the tool returns (note the quoted version, yes and colon strings): JSON { "name": "api", "version": "1.10", "debug": false, "id": 12345678901234567890, "answer": "yes", "ports": [80, 443], "note": "Time: 10:30" } YAML name: api version: '1.10' debug: false id: 12345678901234567890 answer: 'yes' ports: - 80 - 443 note: 'Time: 10:30'

howto: Paste JSON into "JSON Input".
Click "Convert"; invalid JSON shows the parse error from your browser instead.
Read the YAML in "YAML Output".
Click "Copy", or "Download" to get the same YAML as data.yaml.
howtoHeading: How to convert JSON to YAML

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input JSON text Output YAML in block style, two-space indentation, file data.yaml Key order as in the JSON, except keys that are whole numbers, which come first

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: js-yaml converts your JSON inside the browser tab, and the pasted text is not uploaded; the YAML exists only on this page until you copy or download it. An error, such as a JSON parse error, is reported to us as text with quoted fragments replaced, together with the tool name and your browser version.

faq.q: Will yes, no or on be read as booleans?
faq.a: No. The tool quotes such strings, writing 'yes', 'no', 'on', 'off' and 'y', so readers that follow the older YAML 1.1 rules also keep them as text. Real JSON booleans are written true and false.

faq.q: Do numbers keep their exact digits?
faq.a: Yes. A number is written with the exact digits of your JSON: 1.10 stays 1.10 and 12345678901234567890 keeps all its digits. A version stored as a JSON string is quoted in the YAML, so it stays text.

faq.q: Can I convert the YAML back to JSON?
faq.a: Yes, with YAML to JSON. Its reader turns decimals into JSON numbers, so an unquoted 1.10 comes back as 1.1, but the quoted strings this tool writes come back unchanged.

title: JWT Decoder & Signature Verifier — HS, RS, PS, ES, EdDSA
desc: Decode a JWT's header and payload, see exp and iat as UTC dates, and verify the signature with a secret, PEM or JWK key, all in your browser.
ui: JWT Decoder Decode and inspect JWT tokens Decode Verify the signature Verify signature Checked in your browser with WebCrypto; the key and the token are not sent to our servers. HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 and EdDSA (Ed25519, in browsers that support it).

about.heading: About JWT Decoder
about.text: JWT Decoder shows the header and payload of a signed JSON Web Token as indented JSON, keeping large numbers exactly as written, and turns the exp, iat and nbf claims into UTC dates with an expired or not-yet-valid note. It also verifies the signature locally with WebCrypto: a shared secret for HS256, HS384 and HS512, or a public key in PEM or JWK form for RS, PS, ES and EdDSA (Ed25519) tokens. Unsigned tokens (alg none) and a public key offered for an HS token are refused. Encrypted tokens with five parts are not supported.

example.heading: Example
example.text: An HS256 token decoded, then verified with the secret my-secret (the exp note depends on today's date; this token expired on 1 January 2026): Token eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiI0MiIsIm5hbWUiOiJBZGEiLCJpYXQiOjE3NjcyMjU2MDAsImV4cCI6MTc2NzIyOTIwMH0.tSbItJNpja-KxR9Sew4UseTRkf2DxToP11X65NZgLJw Decode and Verify signature HEADER { "alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT" } PAYLOAD { "sub": "42", "name": "Ada", "iat": 1767225600, "exp": 1767229200 } exp: 2026-01-01T01:00:00Z (UTC) — expired iat: 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (UTC) Signature verified (HS256): this token was signed with this key and has not been changed. Check exp / nbf in the decoded payload as well.

howto: Paste the token, three base64url parts separated by dots, and click "Decode".
Read the header, the payload and, under it, the exp, iat and nbf dates in UTC.
To check the signature, paste the secret or the public key under "Verify the signature"; for an HS token, set "Secret is" to text or base64 / base64url.
Click "Verify signature" to get "Signature verified" or "Invalid signature" with the reason.
howtoHeading: How to decode and verify a JWT

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Token format Signed JWT in compact form (three parts); encrypted tokens and unencoded payloads are not handled Algorithms HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 and EdDSA (Ed25519, in browsers whose WebCrypto supports it) Keys accepted A secret as text or base64/base64url, an oct JWK, a PEM public key, or an RSA, EC or OKP JWK Keys refused, with a reason JWK Sets, X.509 certificates, PKCS#1 RSA keys and PEM private keys; a private JWK is reduced to its public part Not checked for you exp, nbf, iss and aud: the dates are shown, the decision stays with your application

Where your token is processed.heading: Where your token is processed
Where your token is processed.text: Decoding and signature checks run in this page with your browser's atob and WebCrypto; the token and the key are not sent to our servers. If you turn on a translation in the language menu, Google receives the text shown on the page, including the decoded header and payload, so keep translation off for real tokens. A failed decode sends us the message Invalid JWT token, the tool's name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Does this tool verify the JWT signature?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the shared secret for HS256, HS384 or HS512, or the issuer's public key as PEM or JWK for RS, PS, ES or EdDSA, then click "Verify signature". The algorithm is read from the token header, and alg none is refused.

faq.q: Is a verified token safe to accept?
faq.a: Not by itself. A verified signature proves the token was signed with that key and has not changed since. Your application must still check exp, nbf, the issuer (iss) and the audience (aud); this page only shows them.

faq.q: Why is my public key refused for an HS256 token?
faq.a: Accepting it would allow the algorithm-confusion attack, where a public key is used as an HMAC secret. An HS token must be checked with its shared secret, so a PEM key or a non-oct JWK is refused for HS256, HS384 and HS512.

faq.q: Why is my JWK Set or certificate refused?
faq.a: The check needs one public key. From a JWK Set, paste the single key whose kid matches the token header. From an X.509 certificate, extract the key with openssl x509 -pubkey -noout, and convert a PKCS#1 RSA PUBLIC KEY to the PUBLIC KEY form.

faq.q: Why does Decode say Invalid JWT token?
faq.a: The text does not have three dot-separated parts, or a part is not base64url-encoded JSON. Encrypted tokens with five parts are not supported. Decode never looks at the signature, so a wrong signature cannot cause this message.

tips: A secret copied from a .env file can end with a line break; with "Secret is" set to text, the verdict says so when the secret matches without it.
If a PS256 token was signed with another salt length, the verdict names that length and explains why conforming libraries reject it.

title: Markdown Editor — Write, Preview, Save as .md or .html
desc: Write Markdown beside a live preview, then download your text as document.md, the generated HTML as document.html, or both in document.zip.
ui: Markdown Editor Write and preview Markdown in real time Markdown # Hello World Start writing **markdown** here... - Item 1 - Item 2 - Item 3 Preview

about.heading: About Markdown Editor
about.text: Markdown Editor is a two-pane writing page: you type Markdown on the left and the preview on the right is rebuilt after each change. The text is parsed with marked, which follows CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown, so tables, task lists, fenced code and strikethrough work. HTML typed inside the Markdown is kept after DOMPurify strips scripts, event handlers and javascript: links. When the draft is ready, save it as document.md, save the generated HTML as document.html (the body content, without a head section), or take both in one ZIP. There is no formatting toolbar and no autosave.

example.heading: Example
example.text:
A task list and a table typed in the left pane; below is the HTML that marked produces with the page’s settings (the page then passes it through DOMPurify). Markdown ## Tasks - [x] Draft - [ ] Review | Step | Owner | |---|---| | Draft | Ana | HTML (document.html)

Tasks

  • Draft
  • Review
Step Owner
Draft Ana

howto: Replace the sample text in the "Markdown" pane with your own writing.
Check the "Preview" pane on the right; it is rebuilt after each change.
Click "Download" on the document.md row to save your Markdown, or on the document.html row to save the generated HTML.
Click "Download all" to get both files in document.zip.
howtoHeading: How to write Markdown and download it

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Syntax CommonMark plus GitHub Flavored Markdown: tables, task lists, strikethrough, fenced code HTML inside Markdown Allowed; DOMPurify removes scripts, event handlers and javascript: links Downloads document.md (your text), document.html (body content only, no head or charset tag), document.zip (both) Length The tool sets no size cap; past 1,000,000 characters the left box shows only the beginning while the preview uses the whole text

Where your text is processed.heading: Where your text is processed
Where your text is processed.text: Your Markdown is turned into HTML by code running in the page (marked, then DOMPurify) and is not sent to our servers or stored anywhere. Images you link to are loaded by your browser from the sites that host them, so those sites see the request. The downloads are built in the browser from your text.

faq.q: Is my draft saved if I close the tab?
faq.a: No. Nothing is stored, in your browser or on a server. Once you have changed the sample, the browser asks before you leave until you download one of the files or copy the whole text, so download document.md first.

faq.q: Does the HTML download include styles?
faq.a: No. document.html holds only the HTML generated from your Markdown, without a head section, stylesheet or charset tag. For a complete page with a UTF-8 declaration, paste the same Markdown into Markdown to HTML.

faq.q: Can I use HTML tags inside the Markdown?
faq.a: Yes. Tags such as details or kbd are kept in the preview and in document.html, but DOMPurify first removes script elements, attributes such as onclick and javascript: links.

faq.q: Does it support tables and task lists?
faq.a: Yes. GitHub Flavored Markdown is on, so pipe tables, - [ ] task lists (shown as disabled checkboxes), ~~strikethrough~~ and fenced code blocks with a language name are converted.

tips: Need a PDF of the finished document? Paste the same Markdown into Markdown to PDF.

title: Markdown Previewer — Check Pasted Markdown as Safe HTML
desc: Paste Markdown to see the HTML it produces next to the source, with CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown rules and unsafe HTML removed.
ui: Markdown Previewer Paste Markdown and check the HTML it produces Markdown # Hello World Start writing **markdown** here... Preview

about.heading: About Markdown Previewer
about.text: Markdown Previewer is for checking text you already have, such as a README, a pull-request description or notes copied from another app, before you publish it. Paste it on the left and the right pane shows the HTML that marked produces under CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown rules: links, images, block quotes, nested lists, tables and code blocks. Raw HTML in the text is cleaned by DOMPurify, so a pasted script or onerror attribute cannot run. The source can be saved as document.md and the rendered HTML as document.html, or both in a ZIP. Markdown Editor has the same panes with a longer starter sample for writing from scratch.

example.heading: Example
example.text:
A link, a strikethrough and a quote pasted on the left; below is the HTML that marked produces with the page’s settings, before the DOMPurify step. Pasted Markdown See [the spec](https://spec.commonmark.org/) and ~~old~~ new. > Quoted line HTML in the preview

See the spec and old new.

Quoted line

howto: Select the sample in the "Markdown" pane and paste your own Markdown over it.
Compare it with the "Preview" pane, where links, lists, tables and code blocks become HTML.
Fix the source on the left; the preview follows each edit.
Use "Download" on the document.html row to keep the rendered HTML, or "Download all" for the HTML and the Markdown together.
howtoHeading: How to preview Markdown before publishing it

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Rules CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown, as implemented by the marked library HTML cleaning DOMPurify: script elements, event-handler attributes and javascript: links are removed Files you can save document.md, document.html (body content only) and document.zip with both Pasted text size Pasted text over 1,000,000 characters is shown in part in the left box; the preview is built from all of it

Where your Markdown is rendered.heading: Where your Markdown is rendered
Where your Markdown is rendered.text: Rendering happens in your browser: the pasted Markdown and its HTML never reach our servers and are not kept after you leave. Pictures referenced in the Markdown are fetched by your browser from their own addresses, which reveals your visit to those hosts. Each download is built from the text on your screen.

faq.q: Is pasted HTML safe to preview?
faq.a: Yes. Before it is shown, the HTML goes through DOMPurify, which drops script elements, attributes such as onerror and javascript: links, so pasted code cannot run in this page. The cleaned HTML is also what document.html contains.

faq.q: Can I share a link to my preview?
faq.a: No. Nothing is uploaded, so there is no address to share. Download document.md or document.html and send the file, or paste the Markdown wherever it will be published.

faq.q: Does it render math formulas or diagrams?
faq.a: No. marked converts standard and GitHub Flavored Markdown only: LaTeX between dollar signs stays plain text, and a mermaid block is shown as an ordinary code block.

tips: Markdown to HTML wraps the same kind of output in a full HTML5 document that declares the UTF-8 encoding.

title: Markdown to HTML Converter — Full HTML5 Page, GFM Rules
desc: Convert Markdown to a complete HTML5 document that declares UTF-8 encoding, using CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown; copy it or save document.html.
ui: Markdown to HTML Convert Markdown to HTML Markdown HTML Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About Markdown to HTML
about.text: Markdown to HTML turns Markdown into a ready-to-save HTML5 file. The text is parsed by marked with GitHub Flavored Markdown on, and the result is placed inside a doctype, an html element, a head that declares UTF-8 and a body. Code blocks keep their language as a class (language-js) and characters such as < inside code are escaped. Raw HTML in your Markdown is copied through unchanged, scripts included, because nothing is sanitized here. The document has no title, styles or lang attribute; add them if you publish it. This page shows the code, not a rendered preview.

example.heading: Example
example.text:
Output of the page’s own conversion code for a heading, inline code and a fenced JavaScript block. Markdown # Notes Use `a < b` in **code**. ```js if (a < b) run(); ``` HTML Output

Notes

Use a < b in code.

if (a < b) run();

Click "Convert", which becomes available once the box is not empty.
Check the code in "HTML Output", then click "Copy" or use "Download" to save it as document.html.

Formats and limits.text: Input Markdown text, read with CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown rules Output One HTML document: doctype, a head declaring UTF-8 encoding, and body; no title, styles or lang attribute Raw HTML Passed through as written, not sanitized Download document.html

Where your Markdown is converted.heading: Where your Markdown is converted
Where your Markdown is converted.text: Conversion runs in your browser: the marked library is downloaded the first time you click Convert, and your Markdown and the resulting HTML are never sent to our servers. If an error is shown in the output box, its cleaned message is sent to our error log with the tool’s name and your browser’s name and version, quoted text and URLs removed, so that we can fix the problem.

faq.q: Does the output include a full HTML page?
faq.a: Yes. The HTML is wrapped in a doctype, an html element, a head declaring the UTF-8 encoding and a body, so accented letters display correctly when the file is opened. A title and styles are not added.

faq.q: Is raw HTML in my Markdown kept?
faq.a: Yes, exactly as written: this converter does not sanitize, so a script element or an onclick attribute in your Markdown ends up in the file. Remove anything you do not trust before publishing; Markdown Previewer shows a cleaned version.

faq.q: Are code blocks syntax-highlighted?
faq.a: No. A fenced block marked js becomes a pre and code element with the class language-js, ready for a highlighter such as Prism or highlight.js, but no colors are added here.

faq.q: Can I convert a .md file directly?
faq.a: No, there is no file upload. Open the .md file in a text editor, copy its content and paste it in the Markdown box; the result can then be saved with the Download button.

tips: To read the result as a page rather than as code, paste the same Markdown into Markdown Previewer.

Where your numbers are processed.heading: Where your numbers are processed
Where your numbers are processed.text: Conversion happens in this page with exact integer arithmetic run by your browser, so the values you type are not sent to our servers. The results are page text: if you turn on a translation in the language menu, Google receives them. When the clipboard refuses a copy, we receive that error, the tool's name and your browser's name and version, not your value.

faq.q: How do I convert hex to binary?
faq.a: Set From Base to Hexadecimal and type the value, with or without its prefix, as in 0x0F or 0F. The Binary card shows the result at once, without leading zeros: 0x0F gives 1111.

faq.q: Can I get FFFFFFFF for -1?
faq.a: No. The converter writes -1 as -1 in hex, keeping the minus sign in every base, because a bit pattern such as FFFFFFFF depends on a register width that it never asks for. For an eight-digit hex pattern, add 4294967296 (2^32) to the negative value first: -1 then gives FFFFFFFF.

faq.q: Can it handle values above 2^64?
faq.a: Yes. It works with BigInt, so 2^64, written 0x1_0000_0000_0000_0000, converts to 18446744073709551616 exactly, and larger values work the same way. A JavaScript Number would round them.

faq.q: Why do I get Not a number in base 16?
faq.a: The value has a character outside that base's digits, such as G in hex, or a prefix that belongs to another base, such as 0x10 with Binary selected. Below the field, the alert lists what base 16 allows: 0123456789…F.

tips: Untick "Upper-case letters" to match code that prints hex in lower case, such as Python's hex().

about.heading: About Password Generator
about.text: Password Generator makes random passwords from the character types you tick, or passphrases built from the EFF Large Wordlist (7,776 words), from 1 to 50 per click. Every character or word is drawn with crypto.getRandomValues, without the small bias of a plain modulo. Each ticked type appears at least once in a password, and an option removes look-alike characters (0 O 1 l I |). After each click the page estimates the strength in bits from the length and the size of the alphabet or word list. Nothing is saved: the results disappear when you reload.

For a password, set "Length" and tick "Uppercase", "Lowercase", "Numbers" and "Symbols"; for a passphrase, set "Number of words", "Word separator", "Capitalize" and "Include a number".

Results per click 1 to 50 Strength labels Excellent from 100 bits, very strong from 80, strong from 60, fair from 45, weak below

Where your passwords are created.heading: Where your passwords are created
Where your passwords are created.text: Passwords and passphrases are created in your browser with crypto.getRandomValues; they are never sent to our servers, logged or stored. The word list is part of the site’s code and loads the first time you generate a passphrase. Nothing is kept after a reload, so copy a password into your password manager before you leave.

faq.q: How many bits does a 6-word passphrase have?
faq.a: 77 bits: each word drawn from the 7,776-word list adds about 12.9 bits, and 8 words give 103. With "Include a number", one digit placed after one random word adds a few bits more, for example 83 in total for six words.

faq.q: Does every password contain each type I ticked?
faq.a: Yes. A password missing one of the ticked types is drawn again, so each selected type appears at least once, as sites with composition rules expect. Every password that qualifies stays equally likely.

faq.q: What does Avoid look-alike characters remove?
faq.a: 6 characters: zero, capital O, one, lowercase l, capital I and the vertical bar, which are easy to confuse in many fonts. The alphabet gets smaller, so the strength shown drops slightly for the same length.

faq.q: Are generated passwords stored or logged?
faq.a: No. They exist only in the page while it is open: no request carries them to our servers, and a reload clears them. Copy a password before generating again, because a new click replaces the list.

tips: For a master password you type by hand, a passphrase of six words gives 77 bits using only letters and the separator you pick.

title: Regex Tester — JavaScript RegExp Matches, Groups, Replace
desc: Test a JavaScript regular expression on your text: matches highlighted with positions, numbered and named groups, and a replace preview with $1.
ui: Regex Tester Test regular expressions — matches highlighted, groups, replace Pattern Flags Replace with Test

about.heading: About Regex Tester
about.text: Regex Tester runs a pattern with JavaScript’s own RegExp engine, the one built into your browser, on text you paste. Up to 5,000 matches are found and highlighted in the text, and the first 200 are listed with their start and end positions and the value of each numbered and named capture group. Ticking Replace with previews the result of String.replace with $1, $<name>, $& or $$. The search runs in a separate worker that is stopped after 2 seconds, so a pattern with catastrophic backtracking is reported instead of freezing the tab. Other flavors (PCRE, Python, .NET) are not available.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Output of the page’s own search code (the worker it runs), with the replacement option on. Pattern, Flags, text, Replace with Pattern: (?<year>\d{4})-(\d{2}) Flags: g Text: Released 2024-03, updated 2025-11. Replace with: $2/$<year> Result 2 matches #1 9–16 2024-03 $1: 2024 $2: 03 year: 2024 #2 26–33 2025-11 $1: 2025 $2: 11 year: 2025 Result of the replacement: Released 03/2024, updated 11/2025.

howto: Type the pattern in "Pattern" without slashes, and the flags in "Flags" (g by default; d, i, m, s, u, v and y are also accepted).
Paste the text to search in the large box below.
To try a substitution, tick "Replace with" and type the replacement, for example $2/$<year>.
Click "Test": matches are highlighted and listed with positions and groups, and the replaced text can be saved with "Download" as replaced.txt.
howtoHeading: How to test a regular expression in JavaScript

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Flavor JavaScript RegExp only; named groups are written (?<name>…) Flags accepted d, g, i, m, s, u, v, y, each at most once Time limit 2 seconds per test, then the worker is stopped and the pattern reported Matches Up to 5,000 found and highlighted; the first 200 listed in the table Replacement $1, $<name>, $& and $$; with g every match is replaced, without g only the first

Where your pattern and text are processe.heading: Where your pattern and text are processed
Where your pattern and text are processe.text: The pattern and your text are processed in a worker inside your browser; the text you test is never sent to our servers. If the pattern is invalid, the error message shown is sent to our error log with the tool’s name and your browser’s name and version; a time-out sends only the words "pattern timeout (2 s)". The message is cleaned first, but the cleaning may not hide everything: an invalid pattern containing quotes or angle brackets can reach the log as typed.

faq.q: Does it support Python or PCRE regex syntax?
faq.a: No. Only JavaScript syntax is tested. Constructs such as possessive quantifiers, atomic groups or Python’s (?P<name>…) named groups are rejected as invalid; write named groups as (?<name>…) instead.

faq.q: Does the replace preview change every match?
faq.a: No, only with the g flag. The search adds g on its own so that every match is found (up to 5,000), but the replacement uses your flags as typed: without g, only the first match is replaced.

faq.q: Can a slow pattern freeze the page?
faq.a: No. The test runs in a separate worker that is terminated after 2 seconds; the page then says the pattern is probably backtracking catastrophically, as nested quantifiers like (a+)+ do on a long text that does not match.

faq.q: Is there a limit on the number of matches?
faq.a: Yes. The search stops at 5,000 matches, shown as 5000+, and the table lists the first 200; every match found is highlighted in the text above the table.

tips: Type each backslash once, as you would between /…/: \d in "Pattern" is a digit, while \\d matches a backslash followed by d.
The v flag needs Safari 17 or later; older Safari versions report it as an invalid flag.

about.heading: About SCSS to CSS
about.text: SCSS to CSS compiles SCSS with Dart Sass, the reference Sass compiler, inside your browser. Variables, nesting with &, mixins, functions, @extend, @if, @each and @for, maps and the built-in modules loaded with @use, such as sass:math or sass:color, all work. Choose expanded CSS to read or compressed CSS to ship. A Sass error, such as an undefined variable, replaces the output with Sass's own message, which shows the line and column. Only the pasted code is compiled: imports of other files fail, and the indented .sass syntax is not accepted.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Expanded output; math.div comes from the sass:math module. SCSS Input @use "sass:math"; $gap: 12px; .card { padding: math.div($gap, 2); .title { font-weight: 600; } &:hover { padding: $gap; } } CSS Output .card { padding: 6px; } .card .title { font-weight: 600; } .card:hover { padding: 12px; }

howto: Paste your SCSS into "SCSS Input".
Pick "Expanded" for readable CSS or "Compressed" for a single line.
Click "Convert"; the CSS, or Sass's error message, appears in "CSS Output".
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save "styles.css".

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input SCSS syntax as text (not the indented SASS syntax) Output CSS, expanded or compressed, saved as styles.css Compiler Dart Sass, sass package 1.105.0 Modules Built-in ones only (sass:math, sass:color…); @import or @use of your own files stops with Can't find stylesheet to import

Where your code is processed.heading: Where your code is processed
Where your code is processed.text: Dart Sass, compiled to JavaScript, runs in your browser once you click "Convert", so the stylesheet you paste stays on your device. Error reports are the exception: when compilation fails, Sass's error message is sent, trimmed, to our error log with the tool name and your browser's name and version, and that message can quote the line of SCSS where the error is. An unexpected failure of the page is also reported, with the same details.

faq.q: Is it a real Sass compiler?
faq.a: Yes. It runs Dart Sass, the implementation maintained by the Sass team, compiled to JavaScript, so variables, mixins, @extend, control flow and built-in modules behave as in the sass command-line tool.

faq.q: Can I use @import or @use with my own partials?
faq.a: No. Only the pasted code exists here, so importing a partial stops with Can't find stylesheet to import. Built-in modules such as sass:math do load. Paste the content of your partials above your code instead.

faq.q: Does it accept the indented .sass syntax?
faq.a: No. The compiler is called with SCSS syntax only, so code written without braces and semicolons is reported as an error. Convert indented Sass to SCSS before pasting it.

tips: Errors point to line:column in your input: fix the SCSS there and click "Convert" again.
Use Compressed for files you deploy and Expanded when you want to review the generated selectors.

about.heading: About SQL Formatter
about.text: SQL Formatter lays out a query with the open-source sql-formatter library, in your browser. It tokenizes the SQL for the dialect you pick, puts each clause (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY…) on its own line, indents columns and conditions by 2 spaces and writes keywords in capitals. Text inside comments and string literals is not changed, and a comma inside a function call such as COUNT(a, b) or inside a string stays where it is. Twelve dialects are offered, from standard SQL to Db2. A query the dialect cannot parse gets the library's error message instead of output.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Standard SQL: the comma inside the string literal does not start a new line. Input select id, count(*) as n from orders o join users u on u.id = o.user_id where o.status = 'paid, shipped' group by id Output SELECT id, count(*) AS n FROM orders o JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id WHERE o.status = 'paid, shipped' GROUP BY id

howto: Choose your database in the dialect list; "Standard SQL" is selected by default.
Paste the query into "Input".
Click "Format".
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save "formatted.sql".

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Dialects Standard SQL, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle PL/SQL, SQLite, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Spark, Db2 Output SQL with uppercase keywords and 2-space indentation, saved as formatted.sql Preserved Comments, string literals, identifiers and the case of function names Errors sql-formatter's own message, which can run to several lines

Where your query is processed.heading: Where your query is processed
Where your query is processed.text: sql-formatter is a JavaScript library that the page downloads when you first click "Format"; your query is parsed and laid out in the browser and is not uploaded. When the library rejects a query, the error text shown is sent to our error log with quoted parts, long numbers and addresses removed, along with the tool name and your browser's name and version.

faq.q: Can formatting break my query?
faq.a: No. The formatter changes only whitespace and the case of keywords. Comments and string literals, including commas or quotes inside them, are copied as written, so the query returns the same result.

faq.q: Which databases are supported?
faq.a: 12: Standard SQL, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle PL/SQL, SQLite, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Spark and Db2. Code Formatter uses the same engine with a longer list, adding ClickHouse, DuckDB, Trino and Hive among others.

faq.q: Does it work with any SQL syntax?
faq.a: No. Each dialect has its own syntax, so T-SQL square brackets or PostgreSQL :: casts fail under Standard SQL, while MySQL backticks are accepted. Pick your database in the list and click "Format" again; the error message often suggests the same.

tips: Function names keep the case you typed (count stays count); only keywords such as SELECT and GROUP BY are capitalized.

title: SQL to CSV Converter — mysqldump INSERTs to CSV Rows
desc: Paste INSERT statements, mysqldump output included, and get CSV: multi-row VALUES, quoted names and escaped quotes are read, one table at a time.
ui: SQL to CSV Extract data from SQL to CSV SQL Input CSV Output Convert Copy

about.heading: About SQL to CSV
about.text: SQL to CSV reads the INSERT INTO … VALUES statements in pasted SQL, such as a mysqldump export, and writes their rows as CSV with a header row. Multi-row inserts, INSERT IGNORE, names in backticks, double quotes or brackets, and schema.table names are read. The header comes from the column list, or is column_1, column_2 and so on when there is none. A CSV holds one table, so a dump with several tables asks which one to convert. It does not run SQL, read SELECT results or connect to a database; the parsing happens in your browser.

example.heading: Example
example.text: A mysqldump-style INSERT with three rows, an escaped quote and a NULL, and the CSV the tool returns: SQL INSERT INTO `users` (`id`, `name`, `city`) VALUES (1, 'Ann', 'Paris'), (2, 'O\'Brien', NULL), (3, 'Smith, John', 'Lyon'); CSV id,name,city 1,Ann,Paris 2,O'Brien, 3,"Smith, John",Lyon

howto: Paste SQL with INSERT statements into "SQL Input".
Click "Convert".
If several tables are found, click the "Convert table" button that carries the table you want.
Click "Copy", or "Download" to save the rows of that table as data.csv.
howtoHeading: How to convert SQL INSERT statements to CSV

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Input SQL text with INSERT INTO … VALUES statements Output CSV, header row from the column list (column_1, column_2… without one), file data.csv NULL empty field Tables one per CSV; you choose when there are several

Where your file is processed.heading: Where your file is processed
Where your file is processed.text: The SQL is parsed by the page in your browser and is not uploaded; no database is involved. Errors are reported to us with the tool name and your browser version, and their text is cleaned of quoted parts, but the messages about several tables or mismatched column lists contain those table and column names.

faq.q: Does it read multi-row INSERT statements from mysqldump?
faq.a: Yes. Every tuple of VALUES (…), (…), (…) becomes a row, across all the statements you paste. A MySQL escape such as O\'Brien and the standard O''Brien both come out as O'Brien.

faq.q: Is NULL written as the word NULL?
faq.a: No. NULL becomes an empty field, the same as an empty string, because CSV has no separate null. Search the SQL before converting if you need to tell the two apart.

faq.q: Can statements list their columns differently?
faq.a: No. All INSERT statements for a table must list the same columns in the same order; otherwise the tool stops and shows both lists, since the rows would not line up. Statements without any column list get the headers column_1, column_2 and so on.

faq.q: Are function calls such as NOW() evaluated?
faq.a: No. Nothing is executed: NOW() is written as the text NOW(). Backslash sequences other than an escaped quote are kept as written, because MySQL and standard SQL read them differently.

tips: To create INSERT statements from a CSV file, use CSV to SQL.

title: Unix Timestamp Converter — Seconds, ms, µs, ns to Date
desc: Convert a Unix timestamp given as seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds to UTC and any IANA time zone, or a date and time back to a timestamp.
ui: Timestamp Converter Convert Unix timestamps to dates Time zone (for the date field and the result) Your time zone (UTC) Use Current Time Unix Timestamp Convert Date and Time Convert

about.heading: About Timestamp Converter
about.text: Timestamp Converter turns a Unix timestamp into a date and a date back into a timestamp. The unit is read from the number of digits (up to 11 for seconds, 12 to 14 for milliseconds, 15 to 17 for microseconds, 18 to 20 for nanoseconds), and the result always names the unit it used. Each result gives the ISO 8601 date in UTC, the date in the time zone you pick (your own by default), how long ago or ahead it is, and the value as seconds and as milliseconds. Negative values (before 1970) work, and decimals are read for seconds only. A time skipped by daylight saving time is refused and a repeated one is flagged.

example.heading: Example
example.text: Output of the page’s own conversion code for a 13-digit value with America/New_York picked; the Relative line is left out because it depends on today’s date. Unix Timestamp 1700000000000 Result box Read as milliseconds UTC: 2023-11-14T22:13:20.000Z America/New York: Tuesday, 14 November 2023 at 17:13:20 (UTC−05:00) Seconds: 1700000000 Milliseconds: 1700000000000

howto: Pick a zone in "Time zone (for the date field and the result)"; your own zone comes first.
Type a timestamp in "Unix Timestamp" and click the "Convert" button next to it, or click "Use Current Time".
To go the other way, set "Date and Time" and click its "Convert" button.
Read the box below: "Read as" names the unit, followed by UTC, your chosen zone, the relative time and the value as seconds and as milliseconds.
howtoHeading: How to convert a Unix timestamp to a date and back

Formats and limits.heading: Formats and limits
Formats and limits.text: Units read Seconds (up to 11 digits), milliseconds (12 to 14), microseconds (15 to 17), nanoseconds (18 to 20) Date range The JavaScript date range, from year -271821 to year 275760 Precision Milliseconds; microseconds and nanoseconds are truncated, and a decimal part counts for seconds only Time zones Your browser’s list of IANA zones, shown under their current names such as Asia/Kolkata Date to timestamp Whole seconds, read in the zone you picked

Where your dates are converted.heading: Where your dates are converted
Where your dates are converted.text: Every conversion is computed by the page with your browser’s own time-zone data; the timestamps and dates you enter are not sent to our servers. If an error message is shown, that message is sent to our error log with the tool’s name and your browser’s name and version, long numbers replaced by a placeholder, so that we can fix recurring problems.

faq.q: Can it tell seconds from milliseconds?
faq.a: Yes, by counting digits: 1700000000 has 10 digits and is read as seconds, 1700000000000 has 13 and is read as milliseconds. The result starts with Read as and the unit, so a date in 1970 or far in the future points to a wrong unit.

faq.q: Is the date field read in UTC?
faq.a: No. It is read in the zone selected in the list, which is your own by default. A time skipped when daylight saving time starts is refused with a message, and a time that occurs twice is read as the first one, with a note giving the second.

faq.q: Can I convert dates before 1970?
faq.a: Yes. Enter a negative timestamp: -86400 gives 1969-12-31T00:00:00.000Z in UTC. Dates before year 1 are shown in the results, but the date field stays empty because it cannot hold them.

faq.q: Does it accept decimal timestamps like 1700000000.5?
faq.a: Yes, for seconds: 1700000000.5, as returned by Python’s time.time(), is read to the millisecond. A decimal part after a millisecond, microsecond or nanosecond value is ignored.

title: TOML to JSON Converter — Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml & More
